pillar: Getting a Cancer Second Opinion at Apollo Hospitals India

items.q: How do I get a second opinion at Apollo Hospitals in India?
items.a:
Getting a second opinion at Apollo Hospitals involves having your medical records reviewed to select the right campus, submitting a structured referral package to that Apollo oncology team, completing a consultation either remotely or in person, and receiving a formal written report for treatment planning.

Patients typically begin by compiling pathology reports, imaging, molecular testing, and prior treatment records, with translation provided for non-English documents. Many choose a remote telemedicine consultation with the Apollo specialist first to confirm the value of travelling before arranging a medical visa and flights. The process concludes with an in-person consultation, any additional investigations Apollo recommends, and follow-up support for insurance documentation. Exact steps and timing vary by case and should be discussed with the coordinating team and treating oncologist.

items.q: Which Apollo Hospitals campus should I choose for my cancer second opinion?
items.a:
The right Apollo Hospitals campus for a second opinion depends on your specific cancer type and the subspecialist depth available at each site, since Apollo's oncology programme is spread across Chennai, Hyderabad, Delhi, Bengaluru, and Mumbai with different centres of strength.

Apollo Cancer Centre in Chennai has the network's most established international patient department and covers bone marrow transplant, gastrointestinal, breast, and gynaecological oncology, while Apollo Hospitals Cancer Institute in Hyderabad is known for surgical and robotic oncology, and Indraprastha Apollo in Delhi is the strongest campus for patients from Pakistan, Central Asia, and Nepal. Apollo Proton Cancer Centre, also in Chennai, is the only Apollo site offering proton therapy. Campus choice should be considered alongside cancer type, stage, and specialist review before travel is booked.

items.q: Is Apollo Hospitals accredited to international quality standards?
items.a:
Apollo Hospitals' flagship campuses hold Joint Commission International (JCI) accreditation, the globally recognised benchmark for hospital quality, patient safety protocols, and clinical documentation standards, giving international patients travelling for a second opinion assurance that clinical practices meet standards recognised across major healthcare systems worldwide.

This accreditation is one reason Apollo functions as a leading private second opinion destination, alongside its dedicated international patient infrastructure. Apollo reports international patients from more than 150 countries, with the largest volumes from the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Nigeria, and Kenya. Because JCI accreditation applies specifically to Apollo's flagship hospitals, patients should confirm accreditation status for the exact campus being considered as part of overall specialist review.

items.q: What support does Apollo provide to international patients traveling for a second opinion?
items.a:
Apollo Hospitals supports international patients traveling for a second opinion through its International Patient Services division, which provides dedicated coordinators, multilingual support, airport transfers, and cashless billing arrangements with major international insurers, reducing the logistical burden of arranging care from abroad.

This infrastructure also includes telemedicine consultations patients can use before committing to travel, and coordinators who assist with itemised billing documentation for insurance reimbursement when direct cashless billing is not available. The level of support can vary by campus, with Apollo Cancer Centre in Chennai having the network's most established international patient department. Patients should confirm which services apply to their case with the coordinating team.

items.q: Do I need a medical visa to visit Apollo Hospitals for a second opinion?
items.a:
Most patients travelling from abroad need an Indian medical visa to attend an in-person second opinion consultation at Apollo Hospitals, and this generally requires an official hospital invitation letter confirming the scheduled appointment before the visa application can be submitted.

As part of the referral process, the invitation letter is issued once the Apollo campus and specialist have been confirmed for the patient's case, alongside guidance on direct flight routes to Chennai or Hyderabad and nearby accommodation options. Visa requirements can vary by nationality and change over time, so applicants should verify current documentation requirements with the Indian consulate and the hospital's international patient office before finalising travel plans.

items.q: How does an Apollo Hospitals second opinion compare to Tata Memorial Centre?
items.a:
An Apollo second opinion generally offers faster appointment access, dedicated international patient coordinators, and cashless billing for insured patients, while a Tata Memorial Centre second opinion generally offers deeper subspecialist volume for rare and complex tumours, broader clinical trial access, and lower cost for self-pay patients.

Apollo Chennai's proton therapy centre also makes it the only Indian private hospital combining proton therapy access with second opinion review under one roof, and Apollo's insurance billing infrastructure tends to suit internationally insured patients better. Tata Memorial Centre's government-funded, high-volume model concentrates subspecialists in rare tumours, sarcomas, and paediatric cancers. Which centre is more appropriate depends on cancer type, budget, and insurance status, and should be discussed with a qualified oncology team.

items.q: Does Apollo Hospitals offer proton therapy for cancer treatment?
items.a:
Yes, Apollo Proton Cancer Centre in Chennai is India's first proton therapy facility, operating a four-room centre with paediatric and adult treatment protocols and offering second opinion review for patients whose cancer type may be considered for proton beam treatment.

Because proton therapy is not appropriate for every cancer type or stage, a formal review of pathology, imaging, and prior treatment is generally required before Apollo's proton therapy team can confirm whether a patient is a suitable candidate. Eligibility depends on cancer type, stage, biomarker profile, prior treatment, and specialist review, and final treatment decisions should be made by the treating medical team in consultation with the patient's home oncologist.

items.q: What medical records do I need to send before an Apollo second opinion?
items.a:
An Apollo second opinion referral generally requires pathology reports, DICOM imaging files, molecular or genetic testing results, and a full summary of prior treatment history, all compiled into a structured referral package with medical translation provided where original documents are not in English.

Complete documentation allows the Apollo subspecialist team to assess the case accurately before recommending a campus, specialist, or treatment pathway, and incomplete records can delay both remote review and in-person scheduling. Exactly which records are needed can vary depending on cancer type and prior treatment history, so patients should confirm the specific document checklist with the team preparing their referral before submission.

items.q: How much does a second opinion at Apollo Hospitals cost?
items.a:
The cost of an Apollo Hospitals second opinion is not fixed and generally varies by campus, specialist involved, required investigations, and whether the patient has international insurance coverage that Apollo's billing department can process directly rather than through a later reimbursement claim.

Costs also depend on whether the review is done remotely by telemedicine or requires in-person consultation, additional imaging, or a multidisciplinary team discussion, and self-pay patients without cashless billing arrangements should expect costs to differ from insured patients. Because pricing depends on the individual case and chosen campus, patients should request a specific cost estimate from Apollo's international patient office, and cost and coverage details should be confirmed with the hospital and, where relevant, the patient's insurer before travel is booked.

items.q: How does CancerFax help patients get a second opinion at Apollo Hospitals?
items.a:
CancerFax helps patients organize medical reports, identify relevant specialists or trials, estimate costs, and coordinate travel, visa, and follow-up support alongside the treating oncology team, from initial case review through to Apollo Hospitals appointment scheduling and post-consultation follow-up for international patients.

This includes reviewing a patient's case to recommend the most appropriate Apollo campus, compiling and translating records into a referral package, arranging remote telemedicine consultations where useful, and supporting insurance documentation and on-ground logistics during travel. CancerFax does not replace the oncologist or make treatment decisions; final treatment decisions should be made by the treating medical team at Apollo in consultation with the patient's home physician.
